    Weights in a cone (toward Proposition 12.8) #

    deformation-refinements.tex: "For each bar differential choose a k-linear right inverse on its image; […] Make these choices separately in each degree and weight". In the family m + Σ_i t_i μ_i the parameter t_i carries the weight χ_i of μ_i, so the lifts are homogeneous when every component has relative weight in the monoid C spanned by the χ_i.

    For a weight grading G and σ, ConeAt C σ n says that the components of n have weights in σ + C, and cpart C σ projects onto them. Maps shifting weights by γ move σ + C to σ + γ + C (ConeAt.shift); maps and bilinear maps whose components have relative weights in C (ConeLin, ConeBil) preserve the cone condition, and their cone parts are clin, cbil.
